items.title: Athletic Bilbao enige club in topcompetities zonder inkomende transfers
items.summary: In de laatste dagen van de transferperiode word je om je oren geslingerd met de ene na de andere miljoenenklapper, maar daar doet Athletic Bilbao niet aan mee. De Baskische ploeg is de enige club in de top vijf competities die geen enkele speler binnenhaalde.

items.title: 📷 OFFICIEEL Union SG verliest aanvallende troef vlak voor de grootste transferdeadline
items.summary: Mohammed Fuseini zet zijn carrière tijdelijk voort in Engeland. De 24-jarige aanvaller van Union Sint-Gillis wordt voor een volledig seizoen uitgeleend aan Derby County, dat op de slotdag van de transferperiode toesloeg.

items.title: Un concurrent de moins pour Lavia : Manchester City dépense une somme colossale, record en Angleterre
items.summary: Du jamais vu, ou presque : Manchester City a dépensé 145 millions d'euros pour Enzo Fernandez, égalant ainsi le record du transfert le plus cher de l'histoire en Premier League. Le milieu de terrain argentin quitte Chelsea, et laisse un peu plus le champ libre à Roméo Lavia, titulaire en ce début de saison.

items.title: PSV, Feyenoord, AZ, NEC, Ajax en FC Twente opgelet: ook UEFA-deadline nadert
items.summary: Woensdag 2 september om 23.59 uur is de transferdeadline in de Eredivisie . Nederlandse clubs kunnen tot dat moment spelers kopen. Maar op hetzelfde moment is er nog een andere belangrijke deadline: het inleveren van de Europese selecties.

items.title: Ayoni Santos is het geduld van PSV waard
items.summary: Met de komst van Ayoni Santos (21) handelt PSV voor de lange termijn. Video-analyse van een rauw, maar enthousiasmerend talent.

In totaal werd naar verluidt voor 4,1 miljard euro aan versterkingen aangetrokken. Dat is ongeveer 500 miljoen euro meer dan in de transferwindow van vorig jaar zomer.

items.title: Mac Allister onthult de bizarre reden voor zijn onverwachte contractverlenging bij Union
items.summary: Kevin Mac Allister verlengde onlangs verrassend zijn contract bij Union Sint-Gillis tot 2031. De Argentijn had gehoopt op een transfer naar een topcompetitie, maar kreeg nauwelijks belangstelling. Dat knaagt, al blijft hij gelukkig in Brussel.

items.title: Football connects communities but can pull them apart if governed carelessly
items.summary: Sport is a space to help youngsters develop character, resilience and confidence, but we need stronger leadership and safer environments to make this happen The fight for the soul of football isn’t just happening in the offices of Uefa and Fifa, it’s taking place on pitches much closer to home. At the weekend games of football for 750 children aged five to six in Scotland were cancelled due to severe behavioural issues within the ironically named “Fun 4s” programme. Seventy-two red cards were handed out in the first week of the season. Accounts describe adults displaying aggression, intimidation and head-butting as if it’s the “wild west”. This isn’t just a Scottish problem. Contacts I speak to in different roles around football confirm and almost accept that “youth football is atrocious”. This should be sounding major alarm bells, for the consequences go way beyond the pitch. The existing disciplinary systems and PR campaigns are not nearly enough to address and change the situation. Continue reading...

items.title: Everton left with only one striker after Balogun deal collapses late on deadline day
items.summary: 25-year-old walks away from £40m deal at last moment Beto and Ndiaye already sold by club to raise funds Everton’s £40m move for US international Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave manager David Moyes with only one striker for the first half of the season. Everton had agreed a £40m deal for Balogun only for issues with the striker’s medical to place the transfer in doubt after the Merseyside club had sold Beto to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City. Enquiries were made to Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham but proposed loans for both forwards were rejected. Continue reading...

items.title: Deadlines, acrimony and a record as Man City back Maresca for Fernandez deal
items.summary: The summer's longest-running transfer saga ends with Manchester City paying a joint-British record fee to bring in midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea.

items.title: Fernández completes record-equalling £125m move from Chelsea to Manchester City
items.summary: Fernández: ‘This is a club built for success’ Chelsea’s move for Monaco’s Camara falls through Manchester City have equalled the British transfer record with a £125m deal to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, who were left raging after their attempts to replace the Argentina midfielder were dashed by Monaco reneging on an agreement to sell Lamine Camara last night. On a day of twists and turns, City emerged in a strong position after they bolstered their attack by signing Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for up to £65m and landed one of Enzo Maresca’s biggest targets on a five-year deal. Chelsea held out for a huge fee for Fernández and it seemed they were going to find a replacement for him as the transfer window drew to a close. Continue reading...

items.title: Sunderland pip Crystal Palace in battle of the private jets to land Malick Fofana
items.summary: Both clubs send planes to France to acquire Lyon winger Sunderland submit deal sheet for £31m transfer Sunderland and Crystal Palace were involved in an extraordinary deadline-day tug of war that concluded with Malick Fofana agreeing to swap Lyon for the Stadium of Light in a club-record £31m move. On Tuesday morning it had seemed that the 21-year-old Belgium winger was heading for Sunderland on a five-year contract, but then Pierre Sage led an attempt to hijack the deal. Palace’s manager coached Fofana at Lyon and forged a strong bond with a player he was keen to bring to Selhurst Park. After speaking to Sage on the phone, Fofana seemed to have changed his mind and decided he wanted to reunite with his old boss in south London. Sunderland, though, refused to surrender. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘A great feeling’: Mykhailo Mudryk seals loan move from Chelsea to Tottenham
items.summary: Deal for Ukrainian winger has £75m purchase option Mudryk: ‘I’m so excited to be reunited with De Zerbi’ Tottenham have thrown a Premier League lifeline to the forgotten Chelsea winger, Mykhailo Mudryk, signing him on loan just before the transfer deadline and challenging him to revive his career. Mudryk became a €100m (£89m) player when Chelsea took him from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023; the deal comprised an initial €70m and €30m in add-ons. Chelsea beat Arsenal to his signature at a point when the Ukrainian was among the most in-demand players in Europe. Continue reading...
